notes: Prompt is tiny (system + 2 short user messages, 217 tokens on the reference capture). Reference response is ~1824 tokens of reasoning+code on ggml-org/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF:Q8_0 with MTP already on (reference timings: predicted_per_second=146.8, draft_n=1946, draft_n_accepted=1465 -> ~75% draft acceptance). Prompt processing is over almost before it starts, so this case isolates decode/generation throughput and MTP draft-accept rate; it's a poor prefill-speed signal (see speed-prefill-agent-semantic-grep-what-time-is-it for that axis).

Prompt is dominated by a real ~40KB semantic-grep RAG dump (message index 3, 'what time is it?' triggered 5 unrelated semantic-grep matches) stacked under a tiny actual question -- ~11.3K tokens total on the reference capture (last_sse cache_n=11332 once cached), almost all of it prompt. Reference response is a single tool call (run_process 'date'), essentially zero generation. Replayed cold (fresh server, empty KV cache) this isolates prompt-processing/prefill tokens-per-second almost in isolation from decode speed -- the opposite axis from speed-gen-lua-tower-of-hanoi. Correctness of the tool call is irrelevant here; this eval only measures timing, never grades the completion.

Short-document half of the summary pair (see speed-summary-long-trace for the other end). Source trace is small -- 6 messages, ~490 tokens of raw content -- rendered into a transcript and wrapped in a fresh 'please summarize the following conversation' instruction (see load_summary_prompt/render_trace_transcript in run_eval.py; this is NOT the trace's own captured prompt replayed verbatim, unlike generation/prefill cases). Motivation: for a summarization-shaped workload (huge input, prefill-dominant, but still a real multi-sentence completion -- unlike speed-prefill's near-zero one), MTP's draft-accept rate might behave very differently on extractive/paraphrase-heavy output than on the code-generation content speed-gen-lua-tower-of-hanoi produces. Pairing a short and long document at the same task lets prefill-time-vs-input-size scale be read off directly while holding the task (and roughly the completion style) constant. Timing only, no grading -- summary quality isn't judged here; a real quality-graded summary eval (its own track, once there's a feel for what summaries are actually wanted) is a deliberately deferred future idea, not yet written down anywhere.

Long-document half of the summary pair (see speed-summary-short-trace). Source trace is a real multi-hour agent session -- 306 messages, ~71K tokens of raw content, ~6x bigger than speed-prefill's own document -- rendered into a transcript and wrapped in the same 'please summarize the following conversation' instruction as the short-trace case (see load_summary_prompt/render_trace_transcript). Same motivation and same caveat as speed-summary-short-trace: timing only, no grading.
